source.title: Efficient Auto-Interpretability of AI Models in Biology

record.tranche_reason: The study tests whether SAE-derived features in a biological model are recoverable and reproducible, and refines the picture of feature stability: some feature classes recur across seeds while functional motifs often do not. It does not test toy-model superposition or feature competition for limited dimensions.
record.gate_note: The study applies SAEs to Boltz-1 and measures feature interpretability, annotation correspondence, and cross-seed and subspace stability. It does not test overcomplete sparse feature storage, interference, polysemanticity caused by capacity pressure, or whether features overlap as superposed directions. Costs and threshold choices used to assess the proposed filtering pipeline are not rows because they measure pipeline efficiency rather than the claim's feature representations.
record.test_reason: The study is mainly a pipeline paper (T4-like), but it reports cross-seed sharedness and subspace overlap of SAE features in Boltz-1, a protein-structure model. These numbers bear directly on whether dictionary features are stable units (V5) in a new, non-LLM setting. It does not test toy-model geometry, capacity, polysemanticity causes or feature dimensionality. Because Boltz-1 is not an LLM, the V4 links are removed.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The authors conclude that cross-seed stability cheaply prioritises interpretable Boltz-1 SAE latents (4.4× fewer evaluations, 5.2× lower cost, about 53% recall), but it favours structural features and drops most functional motifs, so latents should be ranked by stability, not excluded. They offer three unresolved readings of the low stability of functional motifs: real features the filter discards, correlational structure outside the computational basis, or non-linear or non-low-dimensional representations. They call for causal tests at scale and treat the n=5 subspace result as least certain.
record.recipe_differences: The study uses TopK SAEs and measures cross-seed decoder and subspace stability, intruder-detection interpretability, and annotation enrichment. It does not use or reproduce the toy-model superposition method.
record.method_sensitivity: Cross-seed stability and feature recoverability vary by concept type. The discovery uses a stability threshold of 0.5, but the reported threshold sweep gives a smooth trade-off rather than a special effect at that cutoff. Intruder-judge performance is highly sensitive to the output-token allowance: 16 tokens gives near-chance results on positive controls, while 512 restores high accuracy. Prompt phrasing has a smaller but measurable range (0.85–0.97); the three calibrated production variants are 0.957–0.967.

fits_no_version.finding: SAE latents in a protein-structure transformer (Boltz-1) yield residue- and motif-specific features that validate against SwissProt annotations: all 17 residue calls hold, 12 of 16 contexts hold, and zinc and HRD features show 6–114× enrichment.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: V4 extended to non-LLM biological models: SAEs recover sparse, annotation-valid features in protein-structure models.

record.problems: The deployment sweep is limited to 141 density-screened latents from Boltz-1 layer 20; only five functional/catalytic motifs are included in the subspace comparison. The authors caution against strong conclusions from that small sample. Subspace stability measures cross-seed span overlap, not causal use by the model. Some context-validation failures are underpowered, and the secondary-structure annotations are derived from Boltz-predicted structures.
record.rows_left_out: Pipeline cost savings, threshold-selection and cost-accounting results, and judge-harness calibration comparisons are omitted because they measure the efficiency or calibration of the evaluation pipeline rather than feature recovery or feature stability. Other per-feature annotation-table entries are omitted except for the reported zinc and HRD motif results; the aggregate residue/context-validation outcome is recorded in R13.

untested.parts: All of it: toy networks, overlapping near-orthogonal directions, sparsity transition, geometry.
All of it: capacity competition, dedicated versus shared dimensions.
All of it: no neuron-level polysemanticity analysis.
LLMs are not studied. Boltz-1 is a protein-structure model, and the distribution of features across neurons is not measured.
Completeness and canonicity are not tested, nor whether features are causally used. Only cross-seed reproducibility is measured.
Whether superposed features are 1-D. The subspace analysis neither shows multi-dimensional features nor confirms 1-D ones.

missing.what: Class breakdown of the stability filter: it keeps 8 of 9 structural-position latents, loses 4 of 5 functional-site latents and all 3 compositional-region latents.
Within-concept-type correlation of stability with F1 is only 0.09–0.19. This appears only as a note in R1, not as its own row.

record.verdict_notes: The core contribution is a pipeline, so many rows (R5, R6, R13–R18) are method performance or description validation, not tests of a version. V4 links were removed because Boltz-1 is not an LLM; the annotation-validity results are moved to fits_no_version. The subspace analysis touches multi-dimensional features (V6) but cannot discriminate 1-D from multi-D, so V6 is left untested.

versions.untested_parts: Toy networks, more sparse features than dimensions, overlapping directions, interference, and sparsity-dependent geometric transitions.
Whether polysemantic neurons arise from limited capacity or whether important features receive dedicated dimensions.
Polysemantic neurons and alternative causes of polysemanticity.
The study tests SAE-recoverable features in Boltz-1, a biological model, not LLMs. It does not measure how features are distributed across neurons.
Cross-seed and subspace reproducibility are measured, but feature completeness and whether SAE features are canonical units of the model are not established.
The study measures cross-seed subspace stability, but does not test whether superposed features are one-dimensional or multidimensional.

rows.subject: Boltz-1 Pairformer trunk
rows.operation_detail: Correlated cross-seed stability with concept-recovery F1 for 735 concept-winning latents.
rows.measure: Spearman correlation between stability and concept-recovery F1
rows.note: The authors report that concept type confounds the relationship; within a single concept type, the correlation is between 0.09 and 0.19.
rows.check: This is a stability-to-F1 correlation used to justify the prioritisation pipeline, not a rate of feature stability. The authors say it is confounded by concept type (within-type ρ 0.09–0.19). The V4 link is removed because Boltz-1 is not an LLM.

rows.value: mean best-F1 0.84; shared 56% of the time
rows.note: This is the most reproducible concept type reported.
rows.check: Amino-acid winners are shared across seeds only 56% of the time, so stability is incomplete. The V4 link is removed (not an LLM).

rows.subject: Boltz-1 Pairformer trunk
rows.operation_detail: Measured intruder-detection accuracy for the low-frequency sweep, split by stability.
rows.measure: Fraction of latents reaching intruder accuracy ≥ 0.5
rows.baseline: 6.5% of unstable latents reached the bar
rows.value: 9 of 17 stable latents reached the bar (53%); 4.4× hit rate
rows.note: The study reports 17 interpretable latents in the full panel, with 9 in the stable group.
rows.check: This is the pipeline's precision and hit rate in deployment, i.e. the study's own method performance. It also misstates the comparison: 4.4× is the lift over the 12.1% panel base rate, while the lift over the 6.5% unstable rate is 8.2×.
